chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 1 is the only surviving design after Candidate 2 was disqualified for critical safety violations (BPR margin failure). Candidate 1 achieves the required 3.0x residence-time reduction (23.4 min vs ~70 min batch equivalent) while maintaining acceptable pressure drop and selectivity-driven flow advantage.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 is selected as the sole viable flow chemistry design. Candidate 2 was disqualified because its pressure drop (35 bar) exceeded the boiling point reserve (1.5 bar), creating a critical phase-separation risk. Candidate 1 achieves a combined score of 0.745, driven by high chemistry (0.91) and kinetics (0.85) scores, reflecting its ability to maintain selectivity in this EAS reaction. The primary flow advantage is selectivity control via enhanced laminar mixing, which mitigates side reactions common in batch EAS. The user's balanced objective favored Candidate 1's safety and feasibility over Candidate 2's higher productivity but unsafe profile. The main remaining uncertainty is the exact conversion yield at the reduced residence time, as kinetic data was extrapolated. The first bench experiment should verify conversion and selectivity at the design flow rate to confirm the kinetic model.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=1 vs id=2: id=2 disqualified due to CRITICAL safety error (BPR 1.5 bar < required 35.2 bar margin). id=1 is the only safe option.
remaining_uncertainties: Kinetic rate constant k is estimated from batch data; flow enhancement factor for mixing-sensitive EAS needs experimental validation.
Selectivity improvement over batch is predicted but not yet measured in flow.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: Run reaction at design Q (0.45 mL/min) and T (60°C). Sample at t=3τ (70 min) and t=5τ (117 min) to verify conversion (X) and selectivity against batch baseline.
